I think you are on to something, OP. I think there is more difference between now and the 1990s than what you are suggesting, but I agree with your overall premise that the cultural difference between 2015 and 1995 is not as large as say 1990 and 1970, and not as large as what people might have expected.

Here are some possible reasons:

  • Internet - now it is possible to see different genres around the world. While there are still differences, I can see this causing multiple regional genres to meld and converge on each other. For reference, I am early 40s.

  • Digital media - It is easier to share media across space and time (ok, we had radio and TV waves before, but it is hard to share vinyl albums and VHS tapes with people around the world). In combination with the internet, it is now harder for new local and regional flavors to be born and fully develop independently before they are borrowed from and melded with the rest of the herd. For instance, jazz and blues had decades to become an art form before they went mainstream; that just wouldn't happen today.

  • Movies made for international audiences - Movies are still produced by Hollywood, but instead of making movies for a mostly American audience, movies nowadays are made for a much more international audience. This means less nuance, which would be understood by those familiar with American culture, and more explosions, chase scenes, and simplified dialogue, which everyone understands. Call it the Michael Bey effect. IIRC, an opposite effect occurred when movies first had spoken dialogue; prior to sound films, there was a greater diversity of countries and languages where movies were made and then shared around the world. After sound, Hollywood became more of an epicenter and most popular movies were made in English. Movies also had a less frantic feel about them as it was hard to capture dialogue when there was a lot of commotion.

  • CGI - Speaking of Michael Bey, CGI is something that has obviously become more common over the last few decades. It seems more thought goes into the technology than the story/feel of a movie, sometimes. Graphics become better over the years, but it is still the same feel of the movie and flow to a story.

  • Music biz - Several decades ago, bands would begin in garages and have several years to develop their own unique style and sound before they were discovered. Now it seems that musicians are discovered earlier, and often times for their physical appearance as opposed to their sound. The music has a more produced effect. I think this is also influenced by the presence of the internet and digital media.

  • The terrorist attacks of September 11th / terrorism in general - I think this has had an overall stifling effect on creativity, on multiple levels.

  • Generational cycle - If you believe in such things (I happen to), the Millennial Generation would be more conformist oriented than the previous generation. The Millennials would match up with the World War II Generation, which did not stress individuality (think of an old man saying "get a haircut, hippy!").

  • Structured childhoods - It seems like Millennials had a much more structured childhood than previous generations. Children had less of a chance to imagine on their own because they were at an organized soccer practice or in front of a TV. On the plus side, this helped them to stay off my lawn.
